title: Objects
body:
***There are 3 main ways to create an object***
[[Object Literal]]
[[Object Constructor]]
[[Constructor Functions]]

Objects have a property called [[Closure]], which contains all of its accessible variables. 
[[Array]]s and [[Function]]s are both objects in JS

---

> [!warning] The closure line above needs a correction
> A [[Closure]] is not a property that objects have. It is a property of **functions**: a
> function plus the variables it captured from the scope it was *defined* in. The confusion is
> understandable because [[JS Functions|functions are objects]] in JavaScript, so a function
> object does carry its captured scope around with it. Objects in general do not.

An object is a bag of key-value pairs where the values can be anything, functions included. A
function stored on an object is called a **method**, and inside it [[This]] refers to the
object it was reached through.

```js
const car = {
	make: "Mazda",
	describe() { return `a ${this.make}`; }
};
car.describe();          // "a Mazda"
car.colour = "red";      // properties can be added at any time
delete car.make;         // and removed
```

Everything that is not one of the six primitives
([[JavaScript|boolean, number, string, undefined, null, symbol]]) is an object, which is why
[[Array]]s and functions both are. That also means objects are held by reference, so assigning
one does not copy it: see [[Shallow copy]].
